Share SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs (Avery)
Schedule benchmarking session with Atlas test prompts (week of Dec 6) (Ethan/Jordan)
Provide draft pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated proposal (Avery)
Follow up on timelines and procurement contacts (Maya)

meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Avery Lin, Samir Patel (Redwood) — Maya Rodriguez, Ethan Chen, Priya Singh, Jordan Park (Atlas Labs)
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a migration-focused demo for Atlas Labs showing API parity mappings for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood, console walkthrough for model routing, Optimize recommendations (batching/quantization), and security/Dedicated options. Customer asked about latency comparisons, KMS integration, data residency, and pricing for reserved capacity. Agreed next steps: share parity spreadsheet, SOC2 docs, run benchmarks next week, and draft pricing for Dedicated trial.
topics: API parameter mapping (prompt, temperature, top_p, stop, streaming)
Model name/behavior parity between OpenAI/Anthropic/Together and Redwood catalog
Console demo: routing, model pinning, rollouts, traces
Redwood Optimize: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations
Dedicated vs Hosted: latency, cost, data isolation
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployment, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're expecting about 55 minutes. Quick introductions?
[00:00:10] Maya (Atlas): Hi, Maya here - head of ML at Atlas Labs. We run a bunch of production inference for question-answering and summarization.
[00:00:20] Ethan (Atlas): Ethan, platform eng, I own the infra and procurement questions.
[00:00:25] Priya (Atlas): Priya, security.
[00:00:28] Jordan (Atlas): Jordan, data science.
[00:00:30] Avery (Redwood): Great — Samir from our SE team will run the parity walkthrough and demo. We'll cover the API mappings from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, show the console routing and Optimize tooling, and cover Dedicated/private options.
[00:00:45] Samir (Redwood SE): Cool, jumping in. First slide — high level: Redwood exposes a single API for text, chat, embeddings, and rerank. For migrations we map parameters like temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, and streaming semantics.
[00:01:05] Jordan (Atlas): Quick question up front: we use a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic models depending on cost/quality; also a couple of Together variants for on-prem. How smooth is parity?
[00:01:15] Samir: Good question. Parity is pretty usually straightforward at the API layer — the main work is model behavior differences. We provide mapping guidance plus curated model recommendations in our parity sheet. For example: OpenAI "gpt-4o" maps to Redwood's rdx-g4o with similar temperature/top_p behavior; Anthropic "claude-2" maps to rdx-claude-v2-compat. There are occasional tokenization differences, so you want to run a small benchmark set.
[00:01:45] Maya: Tokenization differences — does that affect cost estimates?
[00:01:50] Samir: Yes, slightly. We include token delta estimates in the parity spreadsheet; usually it's within 5-12% but depends on prompts. We'll share the spreadsheet after the call.
[00:02:05] [00:02:05] Avery: We're going to demo a live migration example — two endpoints, one that mimics OpenAI chat completions and one that's Redwood-native. We'll show request/response parity and routing controls in the console. Samir?
[00:02:20] Samir: Jumping to the demo. I'm going to paste an OpenAI-style request: model: gpt-3.5, messages array, temperature .7, top_p .95, stop: ["\n\n"], stream true. On Redwood you'd call /v1/generate with engine param set to the mapped model (rdx-3-5-compat) and pass the same fields — Redwood accepts both chat and text formats and will normalize.
[00:02:50] [00:03:15] Samir: Showing the console now (screen share) — top left we have Projects > Atlas Migrations > Route to rdx-3-5-compat. You can pin model versions, set rollouts (canary %), and configure fallback policies so if a model isn't available it falls back to a cheaper variant.
[00:03:35] Ethan: For production we care about latency SLOs. What are typical p50/p95 numbers for rdx-3-5-compat vs your hosted g4o?
[00:03:45] Samir: On our hosted cluster, for short conversatinal prompts p50 is in 50-80ms per token, p95 varies by model and sequence length. For Dedicated (reserved GPU) you can get more predictable p95 because of reserved capacity and pinned kernels. We'll share the latency profile spreadsheet.
[00:04:05] Priya: On the security side, can Redwood integrate with our KMS and meet our audit requirements? We need envelope encryption, HSM support, and audit logs.
[00:04:15] Avery: Yes — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) integrates with customer-managed KMS or HSM, plus we provide audit logs and RBAC. Hosted customers can use our managed KMS, and we support customer key rotation policies. We'll drop SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
[00:04:40] Samir: Back to parity: here's an example where Anthropic has the concept of safety prompts. We map that to Redwood pre-prompt hooks and also offer a moderation/filters pipeline. The dev ergonomics are similar, just a different field name.
[00:05:05] Jordan: Does Redwood do streaming the same way as OpenAI SSE?
[00:05:10] Samir: We support streaming via chunked responses and long-lived connections, compatible with SSE and websocket clients. There are small differences in event framing but we've included client helper libs to bridge those.
[00:05:30] [00:06:00] Samir: Now demoing Redwood Optimize: we take your workload and suggest batching configs, KV/prefix caching rules, and quantization profiles by model. For example, for Atlas's summarization workload we recommend 8-bit quantization on rdx-3-5-quant with prefix caching for repeated document prefixes — that saves tokens and compute.
[00:06:25] Maya: How does caching affect correctness for conversational state? We're worried about stale context.
[00:06:30] Samir: We support fine-grained cache keys — you can key by user/session plus prefix hash. For dynamic convo state we recommend shorter cache TTLs, and Optimize will surface tradeoffs. Also you can disable caching for certain routes.
[00:06:55] Ethan: For Together models we currently run on-prem GPUs with a custom runtime. If we move to Redwood Dedicated, do we need to change our container images?
[00:07:05] Samir: For Redwood Dedicated we handle the runtime; you don't ship containers. If you need fully on-prem air-gapped we also have Redwood Private packaging that can be installed and configured with your infra team. For Together-style local models we can ingest the model weights and provide a compatible serving variant, subject to license and testing.
[00:07:30] Priya: License and compliance is a big ask. We'll need to review audit trail examples and data residency guarantees.
[00:07:35] Avery: Understood — we'll include our compliance pack and a sample audit log export.
[00:07:45] [00:08:00] Samir: I'm going to run a quick live parity test. I have two calls lined up: one that hits an OpenAI-emulation endpoint (we replayed a few of Atlas's dev prompts) and one hitting Redwood's native API.
[00:08:15] Samir: Pasting prompt: "Summarize the following regulatory memo and list action items" with a 1.2k token doc. OpenAI-emulation returns in 1.9s; Redwood returns in 2.0s with a 3% token delta. Content is functionally equivalent; small differences in wording.
[00:08:40] Jordan: That's promising. Do you provide automated evals to compare ROUGE/BLEU or custom prompt metrics?
[00:08:45] Samir: Yes, our eval harness can run prompt suites and produce diff reports — we've run these for many customers during migration. We'll include an example eval report.
[00:09:05] [00:09:30] Samir: Now switching to console routing — you can create route rules: route by header, route by latency SLO, or route by user tier. For example, route premium users to a higher-quality model and fallback to a cheaper one on capacity pressure. That helps control cost without sacrificing core SLA.
[00:10:00] Ethan: On cost — can you show Hosted vs Dedicated economics for our throughput? We do ~30M tokens/month.
[00:10:10] Samir: For 30M tokens we typically show a crossover point where Dedicated becomes cost-effective around X tokens/month depending on model and utilization. We'll run a tailored calc for Atlas and share it.
[00:10:30] [00:11:00] Samir: Quick note about quantization: for many transformer models, we offer 8-bit and 4-bit profiles; Optimize suggests a conservative profile for generation and an aggressive one for embeddings where quality impact is minimal.
[00:11:25] Priya: Does quantization affect inference determinism for auditing?
[00:11:30] Samir: It can change output slightly; for audit-sensitive flows you can pin the unquantized variant on Dedicated. We also provide model versioning to keep exact behavior reproducible.
[00:11:50] [00:12:20] Samir: I'm going to open the parity spreadsheet now — link in chat: https://redwood.ai/migrations/parity-atlas-sample. We created rows mapping fields and common gotchas: tokenization deltas, stop token behaviors, temperature semantics, streaming fragmentation.
[00:12:40] Maya: Thanks, looking at that now. I see a note about stop token handling differences. We'll need to test our chat completions.
[00:12:50] Samir: Yep — for stop behavior, some models treat stop as a final delimiter, others as a soft probability bump. Our SDK exposes both strict_stop and soft_stop flags to help.
[00:13:10] Jordan: Anything special we need to change in client code? We use the OpenAI python sdk heavily.
[00:13:15] Samir: We provide drop-in client wrappers that mimic OpenAI param names and convert under the hood. For most cases it's a small shim. We also have examples for Anthropic -> messages to prompt conversion.
[00:13:40] [00:14:00] Samir: Now demoing traces and observability: Console shows per-route latency histograms, token cost breakdown per request, and a debug trace that captures the prompt, tokenized lengths, model variant used, and any fallback events.
[00:14:20] Ethan: How long do traces persist? We need 90-day retention for debugging, 1 year for audit logs ideally.
[00:14:25] Avery: We offer configurable observability retention as an add-on. Audit logs and immutable exports can be shipped to S3 for your retention policy.
[00:14:45] [00:15:00] Samir: Switching to a Dedicated example — here you see a reserved pool with autoscaling and burst policy. You can set guaranteed concurrency per-model to protect SLOs.
[00:15:20] Maya: Does Dedicated support our VPC peering and private endpoints?
[00:15:25] Samir: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Redwood Private is the full on-prem option. VPC-based Dedicated keeps data in your cloud account with network isolation.
[00:15:45] Priya: If we go Dedicated, how does key management work?
[00:15:50] Avery: You can bring-your-own-key with our KMS integration; for on-prem deployments we support HSM plug-ins. We'll attach the KMS docs.
[00:16:10] [00:16:40] Samir: Now a short section on performance knobs — batching, dynamic kernel selection, KV cache eviction. For high-throughput summarization, we suggested batch sizes around 16-32 with adaptive batching to keep tail latency low.
[00:17:00] Jordan: Any examples of latency regressions when enabling batching?
[00:17:05] Samir: On small prompt workloads, naive batching can increase p50 slightly but improves overall throughput; adaptive batching keeps p95 in check. Optimize will simulate your trace and recommend safe batch sizes.
[00:17:30] [00:18:00] Samir: Demoing an Optimize report (link: https://redwood.ai/optimize/reports/atlas-sample). Shows expected cost savings from caching and quantization and expected quality delta.
[00:18:20] Maya: Can Optimize integrate with our CI so we can catch regressions?
[00:18:25] Samir: Yes — we have eval hooks and webhooks to fail PRs on quality regressions against golden prompt suites.
[00:18:45] [00:19:30] Priya: I want to understand data flows — when data hits hosted Redwood, does any customer data go to third party services?
[00:19:40] Avery: No — data stays in our processing pipeline and we don't forward payloads to third-party analytics. We can provide a data flow diagram. For customers requiring zero third-party dependencies, Redwood Private is the option.
[00:19:55] Jordan: On the model side, can you version-lock models for reproducibility?
[00:20:00] Samir: Yes, model pinning and immutable model version IDs are supported. You can pin at route level and for rollout you can do canary then percentage-based rollout.
[00:20:20] [00:21:00] Samir: Quick Q/A — Ethan: What is the onboarding time to move our production pipelines?
[00:21:10] Samir: Typically 4-8 weeks for a proof-of-concept migration that includes benchmark runs, evaluation, and a small dedicated capacity trial. For full production migration it can be 8-16 weeks depending on procurement and security review.
[00:21:35] Maya: Procurement and legal timeline is often the bottleneck. We have SOC2 requirement and data residency in EU for some customers.
[00:21:45] Avery: We support EU regions and can arrange Private deployment or VPC in region. We'll surface our compliance attestation.
[00:22:10] [00:22:30] Samir: Live Q: show the API call from an existing OpenAI client shim. Pasting code snippet: client = RedwoodClient(api_key); client.chat.create(model="rdx-3-5-compat", messages=..., temperature=0.7) — almost identical.
[00:22:50] Jordan: Nice. Stream behavior looks identical in your example.
[00:22:55] Samir: There might be small differences in chunk framing as I said, but our client handles it.
[00:23:20] [00:24:00] Samir: Now we'll walk through a short migration checklist: 1) run parity evals on a dev prompt suite, 2) review token delta and adjust prompts, 3) choose hosted or dedicated based on cost and SLOs, 4) set up a routing canary, 5) run smoke tests and production pilot.
[00:24:30] Maya: For the pilot, can we get a sandbox Dedicated with limited capacity?
[00:24:35] Avery: Yes, we can provision a limited Dedicated trial subject to procurement sign-off. Samir will own the trial setup.
[00:24:50] [00:25:10] Samir: Ok, I'm going to run a quick benchmark — replaying 100 prompts from Atlas dev set. The dashboard shows average latency, token counts, and model selection. You'll see the token delta column and a quality scoring column.
[00:25:30] Jordan: Great — that's exactly what we need.
[00:25:35] [00:26:00] Samir: There are a few gotchas worth calling out: stop-token handling, temperature semantics, and special Anthropic safety prompt conversions. We annotate these in the parity spreadsheet with code examples.
[00:26:20] Priya: For the security review, who will be the Redwood contact?
[00:26:25] Avery: I'll be the primary contact, and Samir will support technical items. We'll also loop in our security compliance lead if needed.
[00:26:40] [00:27:00] Samir: Switching to questions from Jordan about embeddings: we can map OpenAI embeddings to Redwood embedding engines — same vector dims for many models; we guarantee minimal delta but recommend reindexing for full parity.
[00:27:25] Jordan: Reindexing is fine, we expected that. What's the recommendation for sparse/ANN indexes?
[00:27:30] Samir: No change there, Redis/FAISS/Pinecone integration remains the same; we output standard float32 or quantized vectors as configured.
[00:27:50] [00:28:30] Samir: A brief note on billing: Hosted is per-token with usage reports; Dedicated is committed monthly with overage and burst. We'll include a sample pricing model in the follow-up.
[00:28:50] Maya: Will you show the canary rollout UI?
[00:28:55] Samir: Yes — under Route > Rollouts I set a 10% canary to rdx-3-5-compat and 90% to fallback. You can watch traces in real-time and abort if regressions appear.
[00:29:20] [00:30:00] Samir: Now stepping through a security scenario: if a request contains PII, you can configure redaction and retention policies route-level. We also offer per-token logs that can be filtered for PII before export.
[00:30:30] Priya: We'll need to see examples of redaction and the regex patterns used.
[00:30:35] Avery: We'll attach the redaction whitepaper and examples.
[00:30:50] [00:31:20] Samir: Wrapping up the demo portion; time check — we have about 20 minutes left for deep questions and next steps.
[00:31:35] Maya: Could you run one more benchmark against a long-form generation? We do 4-6k token generations for summarization.
[00:31:45] Samir: Running a 4k token test now — p95 increases predictably, and Optimize suggests splitting into chunked summaries and using KV/prefix caching. It returns in about 6.3s in this test environment.
[00:32:10] Jordan: Okay noted.
[00:32:30] [00:33:00] Samir: Quick tangent — we sometimes see different hallucination tendencies between model families. For that we recommend eval suites and reranker steps; Redwood supports reranking pipelines as part of the endpoint.
[00:33:25] Jordan: Rerankers — can you run them as part of the same request?
[00:33:30] Samir: Yes, you can chain a generation and then a rerank call server-side before returning to the client. We have support for that in the SDK.
[00:33:50] [00:34:30] Samir: Last section: operational checklist for procurement — SOC2 report, SLAs for Dedicated, data residency commitments, and a support plan. Avery will provide drafts.
[00:34:45] Priya: We'll need a SOC2 Type II and a runbook for incident response.
[00:34:50] Avery: We'll include those.
[00:35:15] [00:36:00] Samir: Ok final live recap: ran parity demo, console walkthrough, Optimize recommendations, discussed Dedicated and Private, answered security questions.
[00:36:20] Maya: This was helpful. Next steps from our side: confirm procurement timeline and send test prompts.
[00:36:30] Ethan: We'll aim to send the prompt suite by Dec 3.
[00:36:40] Avery: Great — recap of our next steps is in the chat and we'll follow up with the parity spreadsheet, SOC2 and KMS docs, and a proposed timeline for a Dedicated trial.
[00:36:55] Samir: I'll own the parity spreadsheet and bench setup, Avery will own security docs and pricing.
[00:37:10] [00:54:30] Avery: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and slack. Meeting ended.
